g.text: Same mechanism as the paper's section 4.2 experiment (there: 0.8 s for a move followed by another move, 1 s otherwise).

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: The gain only appears when robots are faster than planned; when everyone is exactly on time both graphs give the same

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: Planned waits vs emergent waits when robots run

g.text: A and X are lightly loaded and need only 0.5 s per move; everything else takes 1 s, a wait action also 1 s.

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: With waits in the graph, B and D still sit out their full planned waits. Without them, B and D wait exactly

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: as long as the dependencies require, and the gain cascades down the convoy.

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: B2 starts at 2.5 s: X left C at 2 s, but B's 1-s wait B1 must run out first

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: B2 starts at 2 s, the moment X2 completes
